chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Henderson's rehearsal: Goodman charts, and taking over the first trumpet chair
summary: At the rehearsal Henderson ran through arrangements written for Benny Goodman; seeing Autrey given all the lead parts, he moved over beside Clarence Smith, an ex-Jim Europe trumpeter, to the first chair.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah, but he had some bookings. He had a couple of weeks of work at the Savoy, and before the Savoy he had played Christmas -- Christmas eve, or New Year's eve, or something, dance date on 50 -- 155th Street there (unintelligible). So -- and he had several -- I'll never forget this. He had two or three arrangements there. He had made for Benny Goodman, and he was delivering them, and after the rehearsal he asked, Just a minute, fellows. Run this down for me, I just want to see if the notes are all right. I've got to deliver it.

We ran it down, and we didn't stop all the way to the end. And he said, by the way, he said, we're going to work tonight. Put that in the book. We'll play it. Okay. So we're packing up, and we had to rush and get out. I played first trumpet. Oh. I'm a little ahead of myself.
This is not the rehearsal any more.

This is rehearsal. So he kept bringing out, first parts, this to Herman, and I looked down left now, had Metcalf -- oh, Clarence Smith, a very good friend of mine, and a very -- one of the finest trumpet players. To me, he was second to Russell Smith, back with all those guys. He was in the First World's War One, he went to Europe with --
I'll tell you in a minute. Uh, uh, Vodery, not Vaudrey, not Bill Vaudrey.
Jimmy Europe, he was in Jimmy Europe's band. Playing first trumpet, and what a trumpet player! Ohhh! And that's -- you know who that was, don't you? What those guys were?

And he was sitting there playing first trumpet, and he and Metcalf, and I walked in, and Fletcher started giving me all the first parts. I looked around, and I said well who's the first trumpeter here? I said, 'look, since I'm playing all the first parts, why can't I move over to the first chair?' He said why not? I said, 'okay, thank you very much.' And I moved over. Now, that makes me the first man. Now tonight we're working 155th Street there.
I want to interrupt to one extent. Are we still talking about this rehearsal where Leora hears you and says --
Oh, okay. I thought you only made the rehearsal, and that was it.
